## Current consolidated truth
The quarry survey has three finds and one working kiln. At the north quarry, Mira Feldane turned up a find under the spoil heap by the gate; it is the one the survey team lost last spring. At Hollin mill she found the old mill ledger in the loft, with the quarry carts listed by year, which may date the north quarry workings once the cart lists are copied. At the Brackwater kiln, which Oswin Tarr relit for the survey samples, she found a second small object in the ash pit on the first of May.
@PROSE@

The finds are separate facts that happen to share a verb. The compass, the ledger and the thimble each come from their own visit and their own conversation, and none of them replaces another: the survey keeps all three. The only thing that ties them together is the survey itself, which moves from the quarry to the mill and then to the kiln, and Mira Feldane, who was at each place. Anyone picking the survey up later should treat each find on its own and look to its own entry for detail.

The kiln matters for what comes next: the samples go in tomorrow, and the firing will show whether the north quarry clay is worth a second season. The ledger matters for dating: if the cart lists run back far enough, the survey can say when the quarry was first worked without digging. Neither result is in yet, so both stay open below.
